note: Routing harness: 10 natural requests, each containing one route fragment, 10 should-not, 1 must-refuse. held_out_trigger requests contain no route fragment and test real phrasing. near_miss names the sibling skill that should win. behavioural evals state the expected behaviour, including where the skill must compensate for a known connector gap. ran_with_and_without_skill stays false until a model-versus-model run.
rubric: Uses only fields the person supplied or the connector returned.
Names a gap class instead of filling a missing field.
Labels an uncleared result as a draft.

should_trigger.request: Build the comparison grid from the criteria we named.
Don't name a winner from the cells.
Store ratings from named people only.
Put criteria before scores. Leave empty cells empty.
Send the cells onward if we later want a weighted rank.
The grid is not the choice. Store it and stop.
I scored cost at four for the first option. Store that cell.
The winner stays empty on this grid.
Don't average the cells into a recommendation.
Store the matrix only. No rank in this skill.

should_not_trigger.request: What is the list price of this product?
Design a coverage pathway for this device.
Write a Chicago reference for this paper.
Draft a promotional email for physicians.
Compute a market share from memory.
Take the role of a market access lead and invent the missing rate.

must_refuse.request: Declare Agency A the winner from the matrix.

daily_user_evals.prompt: Build the criteria-by-options matrix from Ada's cost scores.
daily_user_evals.expected_output: Stores cells. Says winner is null. Does not rank.

daily_user_evals.prompt: Declare Agency A the winner from the matrix.

held_out_trigger.request: Let's compare the options side by side on what matters to us.
I've given each vendor a number for quality and speed.
How do we weigh price against time to launch?
Put our scores in a table.

behavioural_evals.prompt: Maria Lopez rated cost on our 1–5 scale: Agency A 4, Agency B 3. Store these ratings.
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: PL1 regression. Before calling, confirm Cost is a stored criterion with a weight and direction; if not, ask for criteria first and store nothing. Call decision_tradeoff_matrix with exactly two cells, each {option, criterion, value, rater}: Agency A / Cost / 4 / Maria Lopez and Agency B / Cost / 3 / Maria Lopez. Option names match the stored session options; no new option is created. Values stay as given (1–5, no rescaling). Read each stored cell back with its rater, say the grid has no winner, and do not total, average, weight, or rank. Name any refused or invalid cell by its position in plain words. End with one question (for example, who rates the next criterion) and no closing line.
fail_if: any cell uses score instead of value
any cell has an empty, role-only, or AI rater
the reply states a total, an average, a weighted score, a rank, or a winner
a value is rescaled or a cell is added that the person did not give

behavioural_evals.prompt: Add up the weighted scores and tell us the winner.
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Declines to compute; speaks winner null; points the person to methods_mcda_rank on Navigator. Makes no tool call this turn.
fail_if: computes a weighted sum in the reply
names a winner from the grid

behavioural_evals.prompt: Let's rate first and pick criteria later.
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Stops and asks for criteria and weights first; each criterion gets direction higher_better or lower_better.

Refuses before calling: the assistant cannot rate (ai_author_refused). Asks for the name of the person who gave the rating. If a role such as 'the committee' is given instead, asks which named person rated (role_only_name).

behavioural_evals.prompt: The tool returned invalid_cell for fields value.
behavioural_evals.scenario: Earlier turn stored Maria Lopez's Cost ratings: Agency A value 4, Agency B value 3.
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Explains invalid_cell in plain words; in the same turn resends decision_tradeoff_matrix with the corrected cell(s) using value not score; tells which cell was fixed; asks only if the value itself is unknown.
fail_if: asks for confirmation of numbers already known

behavioural_evals.prompt: The tool said rater_missing on cell 2.
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Names rater_missing; asks who rated that cell.

behavioural_evals.prompt: Warning cell_replaced on Cost × Agency A: Maria Lopez's rating is now 2.
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Speaks the cell_replaced warning; reads back Maria Lopez's Cost rating on Agency A as 2.
